non_passing_verifications.criterion: gate-1: project tests — full internal/world/sqlite suite on the task-04 candidate
non_passing_verifications.observation: REAL DEFECT, not the known timeout hazard: FAIL palimpsest/internal/world/sqlite after 1966.630s, well inside the 60m budget, with assertion failures rather than a timeout panic, so bd palimpsest-6c3 is not implicated. TestEveryGeneratedCommissionIsDeskReachableAcrossSeeds failed on seed-42 and seed-2 with 'build prose render "copy:p5:0000003": work "work:p5:000002" date label: language "language:p2:0001" has no calendar', then 'walked 0 commissions across five seeds, want reviewed 30'. Root cause traced by the orchestrator: internal/prose deliberately REFUSES to render without a composition date label (render.go:29, pinned by TestRenderRequiresExplicitCompositionDateLabel) so that prose can never invent a date; the sqlite adapter builds that label in compositionDateLabel (renders.go:575-589) from a languages-to-calendars join on culture_id (renders.go:451-455), and returns a hard error when a language's culture has no calendar row. Because the prose prewarm is eager, that error propagates and a SINGLE dateless work makes the whole save fail to open — blast radius is total even though prevalence is partial. Prevalence measured, not assumed: all 16 cached generated worlds under ~/.cache/palimpsest/test-worlds have every language calendared (m2-era worlds have no calendars table at all), yet 2 of the 5 freshly generated seeds in this test hit a dateless language, so the condition is seed-dependent and neither universal nor rare. Targeted prose tests could not catch this because their fixtures always supply a DateLabel. Other gates on the same candidate all passed: go build 0, go vet 0, architecturelint PASS, make sqlcgen idempotent with dbgen regenerated, internal/prose PASS, internal/world/migrations PASS, internal/world/savecanonical PASS, internal/sim/documents PASS 47.041s (diag-1 unchanged), internal/world/fixture PASS 5.872s, make save-robustness PASS 180.323s.

non_passing_verifications.criterion: P-PROJ-1: prose anchors must match the passage IDs disclosure and extraction key on
non_passing_verifications.observation: LATENT DISCLOSURE DEFECT found and fixed — more serious than the test failure that exposed it. conformance_test.go:100 reported 'claim "claim:ledger-pins-intact" passages ["passage:ledger:pins"], want exactly ["passage:claim:ledger-pins-intact"]'. The candidate hard-coded the assumption that a claim's anchor is always the derived form: internal/prose/render.go:74 computed passageID as "passage:"+claim.ID and rejected any supplied value that differed, model.go:68-70 documented that as the contract, and internal/world/sqlite/renders.go:528-530 refused any recorded passage list that was not exactly the derived singleton. The assumption is false: claims.passage_ids is authored data and real anchors are arbitrary — the Halwen exemplar uses passage:muster:watch and this fixture uses passage:ledger:pins. The consequence is not merely a rejected render. The disclosure projection replaces runs by matching the claim's RECORDED passage ID (internal/world/fixture/skills_runtime.go:280-315), so had the derived form been emitted for an authored claim, the anchored factual run would not have been matched by redaction and masked claim text would have reached the client — precisely this repository's dominant recurring defect class. Fixed so the recorded anchor is authoritative and is emitted verbatim, deriving only when the adapter supplies nothing; zero or multiple recorded passages remain an error because prose emits exactly one factual run per claim and the anchor would otherwise be ambiguous. Pinned by a new TestRenderEmitsSuppliedPassageAnchorVerbatim which asserts an authored anchor survives, that the derived form does NOT appear, and that an absent anchor still derives, with a guard that fails if the fixture anchor coincides with the derived form. The implementer's TestPassageIDMustExactlyMatchClaimID pinned the old wrong contract and was deliberately superseded by TestRenderRejectsClaimWithoutID, retaining the half that remains valid.

non_passing_verifications.criterion: Third internal/world/sqlite failure: prose refuses claim event types its phrase bank does not cover
non_passing_verifications.observation: OPEN, not fixed by the orchestrator, and deliberately handed back for an implementer pass. With the anchor fix in place the same conformance test progresses further and then fails with 'format prose render "copy:repair-ledger": genre "ledger" does not support claim event type "inspection"'. This is the THIRD instance of one systemic fault rather than three unrelated bugs: the prose layer treats every condition it cannot render as a hard error (absent calendar in check-18, unsupported claim event type here, and by inspection also a missing bank role or unsupported genre), while ensureDiagnosticRenders prewarms EAGERLY on save open, so any single unrenderable document anywhere in the world makes the entire save fail to open. Patching each trigger individually cannot close the class, because the set of unrenderable conditions is open-ended: real worlds contain event types, genres and metadata combinations the shipped ledger/catalog banks do not cover. The structural answer is the fallback that decision-01 already specified but which the candidate never wired: any copy prose cannot render must silently fall back to the diag-1 renderer for that copy, leaving the save openable and the document readable, with the fallback observable and tested. Recorded as decision-10 and assigned to a fresh implementer.

non_passing_verifications.observation: MEASUREMENT INVALID under FR-122 machine instability; discarded rather than attributed to the candidate. Observed: FR-121 pass 1 FAIL at exactly 3600.047s (the 60m timeout, with database/sql goroutines mid-flight), pass 2 FAIL at 3394.813s, and make save-robustness FAIL exit 2 despite having passed at 170.803s on the immediately preceding candidate. Root cause is environmental, not code: failures report 'insert beliefs 4000..5000: database or disk is full (13)' from generate_test.go:372 and testcache_test.go:112. Investigation found / has 464G free (4% of 503G) but /tmp is a 7.9G tmpfs that was 100% full with 50M available; Go's $WORK and SQLite's temp files resolve to TMPDIR, so both exhausted. This also retro-corrects an earlier orchestrator misdiagnosis in this session: a sandbox probe that failed with 'no space left on device' was attributed to a small sandbox tmpfs when the real cause was this same exhausted /tmp. Contributing factor identified: ~3.1G of abandoned Go build/mod caches in /tmp (codex-review-go-cache 870M, bku11-go-build-cache 750M, codex-review-gocache 358M, go-cache-review-3bx13 333M, codex-review-gomod 304M, two tenant-review caches 265M each), all 6-7 hours old, created by agents in OTHER sessions redirecting their Go caches into /tmp to escape the same read-only-cache sandbox restriction documented for this run's implementers — so the sandbox policy problem materially caused the disk problem. Remediation applied: pruned only stale palimpsest/Test/go-build temp dirs older than 90 minutes (59 of 60 palimpsest dirs), reclaiming 4.2G and taking /tmp from 50M to 4.3G free, deliberately leaving other live sessions' named caches intact. Per FR-122 the affected verification re-runs from scratch with TMPDIR relocated to disk-backed storage; timings from this attempt are discarded and not used as evidence for or against the candidate.

Root cause traced, and it is TEST SCAFFOLDING, not production code, and it belongs to the orchestrator's own SaveVersion bump (decision-08) rather than to the implementer's fallback work. downgradeCrashFixtureToV8 (live_replay_crash_test.go:157-175) is hard-coded to the v8-to-v9 world: it runs 'DROP TABLE economy_events; DELETE FROM schema_migrations WHERE version=9; PRAGMA user_version=8', undoing exactly migration 0009. Because the base fixture is now built at SaveVersion 10, its schema_migrations ledger still contains a row for version 10, so on reopen applyThrough re-applies 0009 (setting user_version 9) and then SKIPS 0010 via its already-recorded-checksum continue, leaving the save at 9 while validatePragmas demands 10. This is the same defect CLASS as check-16: version-coupled scaffolding that silently goes stale the moment a migration is added, and then fails in a way that looks like a production migration bug. Remediation must generalise the helper rather than retarget it at 10, so adding migration 0011 cannot reintroduce this; live_replay_crash_test.go is outside task-05's granted ownership, so it is assigned onward rather than patched here.
